numerical_claims.source_evidence: Loans to Customers: 'Loans to customers amounted to ISK 223.3 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by ISK 15.8 bn., or 7.6%, from year-end 2025.' Balance Sheet shows loans ISK 223.3 bn. at 30.6.2026 vs ISK 207.6 bn. at 31.12.2025.

numerical_claims.claim: On the liability side, total deposits surpassed ISK 200 billion for the first time, reaching ISK 201.2 billion at the end of the quarter, up 16.5% from year-end 2025.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Deposits section: 'Deposits amounted to ISK 201.2 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 16.5% from year-end 2025... total deposits surpassing ISK 200 bn. for the first time.' Balance Sheet shows deposits ISK 201.2 bn. at 30.6.2026 vs ISK 172.8 bn. at 31.12.2025.

numerical_claims.claim: Market funding increased to ISK 101.7 billion following senior unsecured bond and additional tier 1 capital issuances completed during the first half of the year.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Debt Issuance: 'Market funding increased to ISK 101.7 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, following the issuance of EUR 150 million senior unsecured bonds and SEK 300 million AT1 capital instruments during H1 2026.' Balance Sheet shows market funding ISK 101.7 bn. at 30.6.2026.

numerical_claims.claim: The total capital adequacy ratio stood at 23.0%, comfortably above regulatory requirements, following the distribution of the special dividend in June and a reduction in the Pillar II requirement resulting from the 2026 SREP results.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Capital Position: 'CAR of 23.0% at 30 June 2026, decreasing as special dividend was distributed in June... Following the 2026 SREP results received on 30 June 2026, Kvika’s Pillar II requirement reduced by 0.2%, lowering the Bank’s total capital requirement to 17.7%.'

numerical_claims.claim: The liquidity coverage ratio remained strong at 276%, and the net stable funding ratio was 137%.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Liquidity and Funding Ratios: 'The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) remains strong at 276%, well above the 100% regulatory requirement... NSFR stood at 137%, reflecting a stable and well-diversified funding base.'
